def _export_grouped_gene_values(_genes, _groupby, _path):
    import scipy.sparse as _sps

    _present_genes = [str(_gene) for _gene in _genes if str(_gene) in adata.var_names]
    _agg = sc.get.aggregate(
        adata[:, _present_genes].copy(), by=_groupby, func=("mean", "count_nonzero")
    )
    if _groupby in _agg.obs.columns:
        _groups = [str(_group) for _group in _agg.obs[_groupby].tolist()]
    else:
        _groups = [str(_group) for _group in _agg.obs_names]

    def _to_dense(_matrix):
        return _matrix.toarray() if _sps.issparse(_matrix) else _np.asarray(_matrix)

    _mean = _to_dense(_agg.layers["mean"]).astype(float)
    _nonzero = _to_dense(_agg.layers["count_nonzero"]).astype(float)
    _n_cells = (

    )
    _mins = _mean.min(axis=0)
    _spans = _mean.max(axis=0) - _mins
    _spans[_spans == 0] = 1.0
    _scaled = (_mean - _mins) / _spans
    _records = []

arguments.environment_rationale: Base image supplies Python 3.13, pip and Debian utilities; /work/venv is created in setup and /work/venv/bin/python is used for all analysis. The source (a scanpy documentation tutorial at revision 8c1463d) declares no dependency pins, so the environment is reconstructed from the exact APIs the code exercises: sc.pp.scrublet in the main namespace and sc.tl.leiden(flavor="igraph", n_iterations=2) require scanpy >= 1.11 territory; therefore scanpy>=1.11,<2 is installed, plus anndata and pooch (both imported directly by the script), igraph (required by the igraph Leiden flavor; leidenalg installed for completeness), umap-learn (sc.tl.umap / sc.pp.neighbors) and seaborn (sc.pl.violin). numpy, scipy, pandas, matplotlib, h5py, scikit-learn, statsmodels, numba and pynndescent resolve as scanpy's own dependencies; everything ships cp313 binary wheels, so no compilation is expected. The exact resolved set is frozen into /work/setup-inputs.json (pip freeze). Inputs: the two 10X h5 files (~43 MB total) are downloaded during setup from the figshare download endpoints registered for DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.22716739.v1, byte sizes and provider MD5s verified against the article metadata, SHA-256 digests recorded, and staged under /inputs; /work/cache is created for potential cache needs, but the reference run itself needs no network or caches because the two input_staging edits load the staged files directly instead of pooch's DOI fetch. The controller runs /work/venv/bin/python /work/reference.py as a fresh process with MPLBACKEND=Agg (agreed - all plotting stays noninteractive; figures are intentionally not persisted, their values are exported), with 4 CPUs / 8 GiB RAM / 10 GiB disk, offline. No GPU needed (CPU sparse-matrix workflow). Estimated total output size is well under 2 GiB (dominated by adata_final.h5ad). Estimated analysis wall time is roughly 5-9 minutes (batch-wise Scrublet, PCA/UMAP and the Wilcoxon rank_genes_groups pass dominate), which must fit the 600 s reference budget; setup (venv + ~250 MB of wheel downloads + 43 MB data) is comfortably within 1800 s.
arguments.explanation: Dispositions: prepare. The baseline is the scanpy "Preprocessing and clustering" basics tutorial (35 code cells, executed without stored outputs). (1) Inputs: the notebook fetches two 10X Genomics filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 files (samples s1d1/s1d3, openproblems NeurIPS 2021 bone marrow data) via pooch from figshare DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.22716739.v1. Setup downloads the exact files from the DOI's figshare endpoints, verifies the provider-registered byte sizes and MD5 checksums, computes SHA-256 digests, stages both files under /inputs and records identities plus the resolved package freeze in /work/setup-inputs.json. Two input_staging edits replace the network-bound pooch DOI registry with these staged local paths; the files, gene-symbol uniquification, concatenation order and every parameter are unchanged. (2) Analysis preserved verbatim: QC flags (MT-/RPS/RPL/^HB[^(P)]) and calculate_qc_metrics with log1p; filter_cells(min_genes=100) and filter_genes(min_cells=3); batch-wise Scrublet; raw counts layer; median-count-depth normalize_total + log1p; 2000 batch-aware HVGs; PCA; neighbors; UMAP; Leiden flavor="igraph" with n_iterations=2 at default resolution and at resolutions 0.02/0.5/2.0; cell_type_lvl1 mapping; Wilcoxon rank_genes_groups on leiden_res_0.50; cluster-"7" top marker extraction. All thresholds, flavors, default seeds, labels and display order are untouched; only append-only exports are added. (3) Exports (15 append-only edits) write to /work/outputs in interoperable formats: the printed per-sample cell counts; unfiltered per-cell QC metrics (violin/scatter data) and per-gene QC annotations; filtering/dimension checkpoints; per-cell Scrublet results; the normalization median target; post-filter gene annotations with HVG statistics; PCA variance ratios; neighbor construction parameters; UMAP coordinates; the marker-gene dictionary; the (cluster, gene) mean/fraction values underlying both marker dotplots and the top-5 DEG dotplot; the complete Wilcoxon DEG table for every cluster; the top-5 DEG list per cluster; the exact cluster-"7" head(5) table and gene list; the final full obs table, per-label counts, and a faithful serialization of the complete final AnnData (adata_final.h5ad: X, counts layer, embeddings, graphs, uns records). (4) Rendered figures are deliberately not captured - their underlying values and identifiers are exported instead, per the export requirement; plots left intact. 17 scientific branches are covered; every artifact appears in at least one branch and every branch's result is exported.
excluded_outputs: Rendered matplotlib figures from every sc.pl.* call (violin, scatter, highly_variable_genes, pca_variance_ratio, pca, 7x umap, 2x dotplot, rank_genes_groups_dotplot): per the export requirement their underlying scientific values and identifiers are exported as CSV/JSON instead; the source's plotting calls themselves are left intact and render non-interactively under MPLBACKEND=Agg.

The per-sample AnnData objects in `adatas` (direct sc.read_10x_h5 loads of the two staged input files) are not re-exported as separate files: the identical data remains in the staged inputs at /inputs and, post-filter, in adata_final.h5ad (layers['counts'] raw counts and normalized X).

#!/bin/sh
# Reference environment + input staging for:
#   "Preprocessing and clustering" (scanpy basics tutorial)
#   scverse/scanpy @ 8c1463d5d97272d5811ad3f4efb57483e23b4c7e
#   docs/tutorials/basics/clustering.ipynb (BSD-3-Clause)
# Input data: NeurIPS 2021 openproblems benchmark bone marrow samples
#   (figshare DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.22716739.v1, CC BY 4.0).
set -eu

mkdir -p /work /work/cache /work/run /work/outputs /inputs

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- python env
python -m venv /work/venv
/work/venv/bin/python -m pip install --no-input --upgrade pip setuptools wheel

# The source notebook declares no dependency versions. It requires scanpy >= 1.11
# so that sc.pp.scrublet lives in the main namespace and sc.tl.leiden accepts
# flavor="igraph" (n_iterations=2); igraph is needed for that Leiden flavor;
# pooch and anndata are imported directly by the script; umap-learn backs
# sc.pp.neighbors/sc.tl.umap; seaborn backs sc.pl.violin. The resolved set is
# frozen into /work/setup-inputs.json below.
/work/venv/bin/python -m pip install --no-input \
    "scanpy>=1.11,<2" \
    anndata \
    pooch \
    igraph \
    leidenalg \
    umap-learn \
    seaborn

# Import sanity check only (no scientific analysis is executed here).
/work/venv/bin/python -c "import scanpy as sc, anndata, pooch, igraph; print('scanpy', sc.__version__)"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- input data
# Download the two input files from the figshare download endpoints registered
# for DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.22716739.v1, verify the provider byte sizes and
# MD5 checksums, compute SHA-256, stage under /inputs and write
# /work/setup-inputs.json.
/work/venv/bin/python - <<'PYEOF'
import hashlib
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

INPUTS = [
    {
        "name": "s1d1_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5",
        "role": "10X Genomics filtered feature-barcode matrix (gene expression), sample s1d1, bone marrow mononuclear cells",
        "url": "https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/40347877",
        "doi": "10.6084/m9.figshare.22716739.v1",
        "expected_bytes": 22848647,
        "expected_md5": "a99285913ea3f3d22600d3d2f8a88e34",
    },
    {
        "name": "s1d3_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5",
        "role": "10X Genomics filtered feature-barcode matrix (gene expression), sample s1d3, bone marrow mononuclear cells",
        "url": "https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/40347880",
        "doi": "10.6084/m9.figshare.22716739.v1",
        "expected_bytes": 20432298,
        "expected_md5": "825f7f7578e3dc0b8955f5a97a402338",
    },
]


def digest(path):
    md5 = hashlib.md5()
    sha256 = hashlib.sha256()
    nbytes = 0
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
            md5.update(chunk)
            sha256.update(chunk)
            nbytes += len(chunk)
    return nbytes, md5.hexdigest(), sha256.hexdigest()


def download(url, dest):
    last_error = None
    for attempt in range(5):
        try:
            request = Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "reference-setup/1.0"})
            with urlopen(request, timeout=300) as response, open(dest, "wb") as out:
                while True:
                    chunk = response.read(1 << 20)
                    if not chunk:
                        break
                    out.write(chunk)
            return
        except Exception as error:  # retry transient network failures
            last_error = error
            time.sleep(min(30, 5 * (attempt + 1)))
    raise RuntimeError(f"download failed for {url}: {last_error}")


records = []
for spec in INPUTS:
    dest = Path("/inputs") / spec["name"]
    if not dest.exists():
        download(spec["url"], dest)
    nbytes, md5, sha256 = digest(dest)
    if nbytes != spec["expected_bytes"]:
        raise SystemExit(f"{dest}: byte size {nbytes} != expected {spec['expected_bytes']}")
    if md5 != spec["expected_md5"]:
        raise SystemExit(f"{dest}: md5 {md5} != provider md5 {spec['expected_md5']}")
    records.append(
        {
            **spec,
            "staged_path": str(dest),
            "bytes": nbytes,
            "md5": md5,
            "md5_verified": True,
            "sha256": sha256,
        }
    )

freeze = subprocess.run(
    ["/work/venv/bin/pip", "freeze"], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True
).stdout.splitlines()

report = {
    "notebook": {
        "title": "Scanpy: Preprocessing and clustering",
        "url": "https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/blob/8c1463d5d97272d5811ad3f4efb57483e23b4c7e/docs/tutorials/basics/clustering.ipynb",
        "source_revision": "8c1463d5d97272d5811ad3f4efb57483e23b4c7e",
        "source_sha256": "9716c6e512d26225b0c6269b49ee01399211ab60b96d523182d66592021000a6",
        "license": "BSD-3-Clause",
    },
    "data_source": {
        "doi": "10.6084/m9.figshare.22716739.v1",
        "title": "NeurIPS 2021 Benchmark dataset (openproblems)",
        "license": "CC BY 4.0",
        "metadata_url": "https://api.figshare.com/v2/articles/22716739/versions/1",
    },
    "inputs": records,
    "python_version": sys.version,
    "resolved_packages": freeze,
}

with open("/work/setup-inputs.json", "w") as fh:
    json.dump(report, fh, indent=2)
print(json.dumps(report["inputs"], indent=2))
PYEOF

echo "setup complete: /work/venv, /work/setup-inputs.json, inputs staged in /inputs"

The reference executes this unchanged and will fail faithfully if the unchanged clustering does not yield cluster "7" under the resolved versions.

The notebook declares no dependency pins, so its original build environment cannot be reproduced exactly. scanpy>=1.11,<2 (resolved during setup and frozen in /work/setup-inputs.json) is used; cluster numbering/identities may be version-sensitive (igraph Leiden, HVG tie-handling, Scrublet/UMAP defaults) even though all parameters, seeds and defaults used by the source are preserved.

All marker genes listed in marker_genes are assumed to survive the notebook's own gene filtering (min_cells=3), consistent with the rendered tutorial; if any are absent, only genes present in adata.var_names appear in the marker dotplot value exports (and in what the dotplot itself can display).

The figshare download endpoints (ndownloader.figshare.com/files/40347877 and /40347880) are assumed to serve the DOI's original files during setup; byte sizes and provider MD5s are verified and SHA-256 recorded (the source receipt had not previously verified them against an actual download).

Determinism relies on scanpy's default random_state settings (0 for Scrublet, neighbors/UMAP and the Leiden flavors) as used implicitly by the source; the plan adds no seeds and changes no randomness handling.

The reference run is estimated at roughly 5-9 minutes on 4 CPUs / 8 GiB (dominated by batch-wise Scrublet, PCA/UMAP and the all-gene Wilcoxon rank_genes_groups). It is assumed to fit the 600 s budget; if it does not, that is a resource-limit failure that cannot be repaired without changing the source science.

adata.write_h5ad at the very end is assumed to serialize the accumulated uns records (e.g. uns['scrublet'], uns['rank_genes_groups'], uns['pca']) with the resolved anndata version, as is standard for scanpy results; it is deliberately the last statement so all other artifacts are already on disk if serialization of this one bonus export were to fail.
